note: Lesson 7.3 (migration) is a process; the cleaning workflow is shown as steps.

walk.title: Solve it: moving Kora's records without breaking them

steps.say: Eleven spreadsheets, eighteen thousand four hundred rows, and the same agent spelled three ways. We move only what's worth keeping, and we prove it arrived.
A staff table maps every agent name used in the sheets to one user email. The mapping sheet covers all seventy-four columns: forty-one mapped, thirty-three dropped with reasons.
show: Bisi · Bisola A. · BA → one email

steps.say: One repeatable n8n workflow cleans everything: trim, lowercase emails, phones to plus two three four, budgets to numbers, stages to exact labels.
show: Bad rows → rejects, with a reason

steps.say: De-duplicate on strong keys: email first, then phone. Name-only matches go to a review tab, and the office managers clear them in two afternoons.
Test loads into a sandbox: twenty of each object, then ten percent. Two mapping errors are found and fixed before the real load.
Cutover weekend. Friday the sheets freeze and the full load runs. Saturday we reconcile and make the go decision. Monday the hypercare desk opens.

walk.end: That's the migration: mapped, cleaned, de-duplicated, tested and reconciled, with a rollback plan if anything fails.
